subject: Order form — payment cadence, taxes & signature timeline (Acme)
messages:
From: Lena Torres <lena.torres@acme.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: greg.adams@acme.com, procurement@acme.com
Date: 2027-06-05T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Order form: payment cadence and tax allocation — Acme

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Procurement has a few clarifications before we can route to our CFO for signature:

- Payment cadence: we need the ability to split the committed spend into three invoices over 12 months rather than a single up-front invoice. Can you confirm Redwood can accommodate staged invoicing?
- Net terms: Acme typically needs Net 60 on new vendors. Is there flexibility here or an early-pay discount?
- Taxes: our tax team is asking whether Redwood will gross up for VAT/GST or if Acme will be responsible for indirect taxes.
- Exhibit B / Pricing: we'd like pricing tiers for usage above the commit (see note 3 in the attached).

I attached a short note with our procurement team's asks (ACME_Amend_OrderForm_Requests.pdf).

Can we get proposed language and a target signing timeline? Ideally we close before June 18 so we can hit our Q2 budget window.

Thanks,
Lena Torres
Sourcing Manager, Acme Corporation
Lena.Torres@acme.com

--
Attachment: ACME_Amend_OrderForm_Requests.pdf (1 page PDF, summary of asks)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Lena Torres <lena.torres@acme.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-05T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form: payment cadence and tax allocation — Acme

Lena — thanks for the clear list. Looping in legal and finance to weigh the options; copying Karthik for commercial alignment.

High-level response / next steps:
1) Staged invoicing: we can support a 3-installment invoicing schedule tied to contract commencement + 4 months + 8 months. Need legal to confirm language for how the minimum commitment is allocated across invoices.
2) Net terms: our standard for new enterprise customers is Net 30, but we can discuss a Net 60 with a modest surcharge or an early-pay discount. Lauren — any objections to offering Net 60 in exchange for a 1% early-pay discount within 10 days?
3) Taxes: Redwood's preference is to treat taxes as the customer's responsibility unless local law requires withholding/gross-up. Lauren — please advise on required language for VAT/GST/withholding.
4) Exhibit B: attaching an initial pricing exhibit that includes tiered overage rates; Acme, please review and flag any materially different numbers.

I've attached Redwood's redlined Order Form and the draft Exhibit B pricing for your review. If we can align on language by EOD Tuesday (6/8), I'll circulate a clean doc for signature and send a DocuSign envelope.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: Redwood_OrderForm_Redlines.docx, ExhibitB_pricing_v1.xlsx

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-06T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form: payment cadence and tax allocation — Acme

Marissa / team — I reviewed the redlines and Acme's asks and have the following draft positions for negotiation. I've attached a short comments doc with proposed text (LF_comments_orderform_redlines.docx).

1) Definitions / Minimum Commitment: define "Committed Spend" as the total dollars invoiced in the first 12 months. For staged invoicing, include explicit proration language: if contract starts mid-month, the first invoice will be pro rata. Avoid any wording that allows retroactive crediting of unused committed spend.

2) Invoicing & Payment Terms: Redwood standard is Net 30. If commercial is comfortable offering Net 60 to close, require an 1% early-payment discount (payment within 10 days) and a 2% surcharge if payment > 61 days. Alternatively, we can offer Net 30 with 30-day payment milestone schedule across the three invoices.

3) Taxes & Withholding: propose clause that client is responsible for all sales, use, VAT/GST, and similar taxes, excluding Redwood's income taxes. For jurisdictions that require withholding, include a gross-up obligation only where required by law and limited to the lesser of gross-up or tax credit mechanics. Also require customer's tax ID and invoicing evidence prior to first invoice if they claim tax-exempt status.

4) Exhibit B / Overage Pricing: recommend locking tiered rates for the first 12 months and allowing Redwood to revisit pricing at 12-month renewal with 60 days' notice. For overage calculation, bill actual consumption rounded to nearest 1000 tokens.

5) PO & Billing Contact: request Acme provide a Purchase Order number and a dedicated billing contact to avoid invoice delays.

6) Signature timeline: if commercial can confirm acceptance of the above by EOD 6/8, legal can issue a clean order form for signature by 6/10 and route DocuSign for execution by 6/11.

No legal red flags on the material commercial asks; main negotiation points are Net terms and tax gross-up mechanics.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

--
Attachment: LF_comments_orderform_redlines.docx

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Lena Torres <lena.torres@acme.com>, Greg Adams <greg.adams@acme.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-07T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form: payment cadence and tax allocation — Acme

Lena / Greg — thanks for the patience. Quick summary and proposed path forward so we have everything in writing: 

1) Staged invoicing: Redwood will accept a 3-invoice schedule (commencement, month 4, month 8). Legal has inserted proration language — see LF_comments_orderform_redlines.docx for exact text.

2) Net terms: to keep momentum, Redwood is willing to accept Net 60 for Acme on this order provided we add a 1% early-pay discount if paid within 10 days of invoice. If Acme prefers no discount, we can alternatively do Net 30 with no surcharge. Please confirm preference.

3) Taxes: Redwood's position is that Acme will be responsible for VAT/GST/sales taxes. Where local law requires withholding, we'll accept a limited gross-up or tax credit approach per Lauren's language. We'll need Acme's tax IDs and billing contact prior to first invoice.

4) Exhibit B pricing: attached is the current Exhibit B with tiered overage rates; Karthik will review any material changes you call out.

5) Timeline & signature: Lauren has confirmed legal can produce a clean Order Form for signature if we align on the items above by EOD Tuesday (2027-06-08). Proposed sign date: no later than 2027-06-14. I'll issue a DocuSign envelope once you confirm the net terms and tax approach.

Action items for Acme: confirm (a) preferred payment term: Net 60 with 1% early-pay discount OR Net 30 no discount; (b) OK with client-responsible taxes + gross-up only where required by law; (c) provide billing contact and PO number.

If you want to do a short call to close this out, I'm available 6/8 between 9–11 PT.

Thanks,
Marissa
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192
